questions.stem: A factory discharges warm water from its cooling systems into a river. Fish populations downstream decline, despite the water containing no toxic chemicals. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: The warm water makes the fish too active, so they die of exhaustion
Warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen, so fish cannot obtain enough oxygen for respiration and suffocate
The warm water causes excessive plant growth that blocks the river
Fish prefer cold water because it contains more food

questions.explanation: This is thermal pollution. Warmer water has a lower capacity to hold dissolved oxygen (oxygen is less soluble at higher temperatures). Fish and other aquatic organisms need dissolved oxygen for aerobic respiration. When oxygen levels drop below a critical threshold, fish suffocate. Additionally, warmer temperatures increase the metabolic rate of fish, meaning they need MORE oxygen while less is available.

questions.stem: Deforestation of tropical rainforests contributes to climate change, soil erosion, and biodiversity loss. A student argues that replanting trees (reforestation) can completely reverse these effects. Why is this argument oversimplified?

options.text: Reforestation is impossible because trees cannot grow where forests have been cut
While reforestation helps absorb CO2, it takes decades for new forests to reach the biodiversity and carbon storage capacity of old-growth forests, and many extinct species cannot be brought back
Replanted trees produce more CO2 than they absorb
Reforestation only works in temperate regions, not tropical ones

questions.explanation: Reforestation is beneficial but cannot fully reverse the damage of deforestation. Old-growth rainforests have taken hundreds of years to develop their complex ecosystems. Replanted forests take decades to mature and may never achieve the same biodiversity. Species that have gone extinct are permanently lost. Soil that has eroded may take centuries to reform. Reforestation helps, but prevention of deforestation is far more effective.

questions.stem: Pesticides sprayed on crops can enter food chains. DDT was found in very high concentrations in the bodies of birds of prey at the top of food chains, even though only small amounts were sprayed. What process explains this?

options.text: The birds of prey directly ate the pesticide from the fields
Bioaccumulation - DDT is not broken down or excreted, so it accumulates in organisms and becomes more concentrated at each trophic level
The DDT was attracted to birds of prey because of their body heat
Birds of prey produce DDT naturally in their bodies

questions.explanation: Bioaccumulation occurs when a persistent substance (like DDT) is absorbed faster than it is broken down or excreted. At each trophic level, predators consume many prey organisms, accumulating the DDT from all of them. This means concentrations increase dramatically up the food chain (biomagnification). Top predators like birds of prey end up with dangerously high concentrations, causing egg shell thinning and population decline.

questions.stem: Peat bogs store large amounts of carbon in partially decomposed plant material. Burning peat for fuel or draining peat bogs for agriculture releases this stored carbon. Why is the destruction of peat bogs particularly damaging in terms of climate change?

options.text: Peat bogs are too small to make any difference to atmospheric CO2
Peat bogs have accumulated carbon over thousands of years; destroying them releases this ancient carbon rapidly as CO2, and eliminates the bog's ability to continue sequestering carbon
Peat bogs release methane, which cools the atmosphere
Peat bogs only store nitrogen, not carbon

questions.explanation: Peat bogs are significant carbon stores, having accumulated partially decomposed plant material over thousands of years in waterlogged, acidic, low-oxygen conditions. When peat is drained or burned, this stored carbon is released rapidly as CO2. Additionally, the destroyed bog can no longer sequester carbon. Peat bogs globally store more carbon than all the world's forests combined, making their protection vital.

questions.stem: An indicator species is an organism whose presence or absence tells us about environmental conditions. Bloodworms (which tolerate low oxygen) are found in large numbers in a river, but mayfly larvae (which need high oxygen) are absent. What does this indicate about the river?

options.text: The river is clean and well-oxygenated
The river is likely polluted with organic waste, resulting in low dissolved oxygen levels
The river is too cold for mayfly larvae
Bloodworms have eaten all the mayfly larvae

questions.explanation: Bloodworms are indicator species for polluted, low-oxygen water. They have haemoglobin (hence their red colour) that helps them survive in oxygen-poor conditions. Mayfly larvae require clean, oxygen-rich water and cannot survive in polluted conditions. The presence of bloodworms and absence of mayflies strongly indicates organic pollution (e.g., sewage), which causes bacterial decomposition that depletes dissolved oxygen.
